about: Backported features from the FM-1 scene: one build switch each (firmware/src/backports.h; tools/build.py passes FELUCCA_x=0/1). Costs measured on feat/backports-features in the fitting config (FELUCCA_SAMPLES_SKIP=SCRCH FELUCCA_DLY_LEN=32768): the switch alone on, minus the same build with every backport switch at 0 (base 571,328 B flash, RAM 92,480 B, pool 282,192 B, RAMTEXT 32,016 B). A switch at 0 builds code and data identical to the tree without the feature (checked per feature by comparing the ELF sections). The builder shows 'notice' next to the switch; 'warning': true marks an item it must show as a WARNING (X0X-derived or experimental). X0X-derived items carry warning: true and a notice in the form 'Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0). Experimental in Optimist; ...'.

items.title: Motion recording: knob moves recorded per step (SEQ > MOTION)

source.author: Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments
source.files: firmware/src/motion.c (the 64-event store, base / active, motion_capture, motion_step), hooks in seq.c, ui_input.c, project.c

files: hooks: seq.c (motion_step, motion_begin / motion_end), project.c (capture / apply / flash), params.c MOTION page, ui_draw.c, ui_input.c (knobs, page)

cost.cpu: per step of a track with motion on: a scan of <= 64 records (sequencer, not the render)

items.storage: No project format change (FUN8 is 3,840 B = the whole sector payload). The store (200 B: the project's sum, count, on bits, 64 x 3-byte events) lives beside each project buffer in RAM (pool: 4 slots + autosave + the song's backup) and in flash in the unused bytes 32..255 of the project's own sector (between the 32-byte commit header and the payload at 256): a 208-byte record (magic, store, CRC) programmed after the project's commit; read back only when its CRC holds and its sum is the loaded project's. A build without the switch ignores it, and its next save of that slot drops it. feat/drum-sends (FUNA: lanes in their own record at 0xE5000/0xE6000, a 4-byte key in the project) keeps the 256-byte payload offset and the 32-byte header, so the 208 B still fit (16 B spare).
items.limits: 64 events for the four tracks together (Felucca's limit); values -128..127 (every recordable parameter fits); a live section stored while playing and reset before it reached flash loses its motion; not editable from the web editor; motion edits are not undoable
items.notice: Motion recording after Felucca 1.0 by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0).

tools/build.py (the float unit, X0X's FPU flags, only with the switch)

cost.cpu: emulator (perf/acid, FELUCCA_BENCH 5..7: the 16-step line in sixteenths), per sample of a sounding part ~315 instructions (was ~407 before perf/acid; one part 137 per audio sample, three parts with Soft drive and square 520); the emulator counts one instruction per FPU operation: real FPU latencies unmeasured; X0X reports 433..465 instr/sample per 303 on its host with 2x oversampling

items.limits: EXPERIMENTAL: the first float code in this firmware (its own unit, X0X's -mcpu=r3 -mfprev1; only the audio ISR runs it); X0X ran it on a real FM-1 [R], not tried here on hardware; no pitch bend / LFO pitch / TUNE on the 303; X0X's overload guard (lite mode) not wired; TB-3PO's six scales reduced to minor from the track's ROOT; 4 presets
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0). Experimental in Optimist; float DSP, emulator-tested only, ~14.7 KB of flash. Open303 by Robin Schmidt (MIT), TB-3PO after the Phazerville Hemisphere Suite (GPL-3.0).
